newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia vows to pursue stable currency.
newsitem.headline: Croatia vows to pursue stable currency.

text.p: Croatia will uphold its stable currency, kuna, in 1997 and continue the low inflation policy despite widespread insolvency and shrinking exports, Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro said on Wednesday.
The news agency HINA quoted Skegro telling a Chamber of Commerce meeting that Croatia achieved 10 percent economic growth in 1996, while industrial output had been rising for the last 14 months.

But economist Branimir Lokin, a member of the chamber, told the meeting overall exports had fallen 10 percent in 1996, with an over-strong kuna and widespread company insolvency still plaguing the economy.
Croatia launched an economic austerity programme after introducing the kuna in 1993, which effectively slashed inflation.
It also aims to start talks on admittance to the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA), Skegro said. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
